events.title: The future Emperor Augustus is born in Rome
events.description: Gaius Octavius was born in Rome, great-nephew of Julius Caesar. As Augustus he ended the civil wars and turned the Republic into a monarchy that lasted for centuries.
events.html: Gaius Octavius was born in Rome, great-nephew of Julius Caesar. As Augustus he ended the civil wars and turned the Republic into a monarchy that lasted for centuries.

events.title: Pope Callixtus II and Henry V agree the Concordat of Worms
events.description: At Worms, Pope Callixtus II and Emperor Henry V ended the Investiture Controversy. The emperor gave up investing bishops with ring and staff, while in Germany elections were held in his presence and he granted the elected bishop the regalia.

events.title: The French defeat the English at the Battle of Arnemuiden
events.description: At the start of the Hundred Years' War, a French force defeated the English in the war's first naval battle. It was the first recorded European naval battle using artillery: the English ship Christopher carried three cannons and one handgun.

events.title: The Yorkists win the Battle of Blore Heath
events.description: At Blore Heath in Staffordshire, near Market Drayton, the Yorkists won a battle of the Wars of the Roses, the struggle between the houses of Lancaster and York for the English throne that lasted until 1487.
events.html: At Blore Heath in Staffordshire, near Market Drayton, the Yorkists won a battle of the Wars of the Roses, the struggle between the houses of Lancaster and York for the English throne that lasted until 1487.

events.title: The Royalists win the skirmish at Powick Bridge
events.description: In the first engagement between the principal field armies of the Royalists and Parliamentarians, Prince Rupert's Royalist force defeated a Parliamentarian detachment under Colonel John Brown south of Worcester. Brown had been sent to capture a Royalist convoy of valuables.

events.title: John Paul Jones captures HMS Serapis off Flamborough Head
events.description: In a brutal moonlit battle, John Paul Jones's sinking Bonhomme Richard captured HMS Serapis off Yorkshire. His later-reported reply 'I have not yet begun to fight' became a naval legend.

events.title: Johann Galle discovers Neptune
events.description: At the Berlin Observatory, Johann Galle found Neptune within a degree of where Urbain Le Verrier had calculated. It was the first planet found by mathematical prediction.

events.title: Sigmund Freud dies in London
events.description: Freud, who had fled Nazi-occupied Vienna the year before, died aged 83 after his doctor gave him lethal doses of morphine at his request. His theories of the unconscious reshaped twentieth-century thought.
